title: Ring all-reduce
brief: Implement ring all-reduce from point-to-point isend and irecv across processes on the gloo backend, check it against dist.all_reduce, and write the alpha-beta cost model that predicts what it costs on NVLink, PCIe, and InfiniBand.
hints: Start with the model. transfer_time is alpha + n / (B * 1e9), and a ring all-reduce is 2 (p - 1) of those with n / p bytes each. The tests check your answer against the 6.26 ms that 1 GiB takes on 8 ranks at 300 GB/s per direction.
The tests run five short jobs, each starting 2 to 4 processes, so allow about half a minute. This lab runs on CPU tensors with the gloo backend; the GPU isn't used.
A blocking dist.send in every rank deadlocks, because nobody is receiving. Post dist.isend and dist.irecv together, then wait on both. A deadlock shows up as a timeout, not a hang.
In reduce-scatter, receive into a scratch buffer and add it to your chunk after the wait. In all-gather, receive straight into the slice x[lo:hi]; no scratch is needed.
Chunk indices wrap around the ring: use (rank - step) % p. When n is smaller than p, some chunks are empty, so skip the send and the receive for those.
The test counts the bytes you send by wrapping dist.isend and dist.send. Rank r should send 2 (p - 1) / p of the array, so a ring that sends the whole array each step fails the byte check.

Your measured ring is Python calling gloo, so it isn't a hardware benchmark. Compare ring_busbw_gbs with builtin_busbw_gbs, and the fitted fit_bandwidth_gbs with the NVLink and PCIe rates in the table.
